Question: Three distinct integers are selected at random between \(1\) and \(2016,\) inclusive. Which of the following is a correct statement about the probability \(p\) that the product of the three integers is odd?
Solution:
A product of integers is odd exactly when every factor is odd. There are \(1008\) odd integers among \(1,2,\ldots,2016\).

Imagine selecting the three integers one at a time without replacement. Each unordered selection can arise in exactly six orders, so this gives the same probability as selecting three distinct integers together.

The first selection is odd with probability \(1008/2016=1/2\). If it is odd, then \(1007\) of the remaining \(2015\) integers are odd. If the first two selections are odd, then \(1006\) of the remaining \(2014\) integers are odd. Therefore
\[
p=\frac12\cdot\frac{1007}{2015}\cdot\frac{1006}{2014}.
\]
Removing odd integers makes each later odd-selection probability less than one-half. Indeed,
\[
2(1007)<2015,
\qquad 2(1006)<2014.
\]
Consequently,
\[
p<\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac18.
\]
The correct statement is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
